description: Promise-based process-tree termination for Node.js on Windows and POSIX. killTree(pid, options) resolves with a typed result, rejects with KillTreeError codes, supports AbortSignal, and can escalate to SIGKILL after a grace period.
rules: Import { killTree } from 'quiet-kill-tree' and await it; there is no callback form.
Check result.killed before treating teardown as a failure: a gone pid resolves with killed: false and reason 'not-found' or 'already-exited'.
Catch KillTreeError and branch on error.code ('EACCES', 'ETIMEDOUT', 'ESPAWN', 'EPARSE', 'EFAILED', 'EREFUSED', 'EABORTED'); never parse the message text.
Pass timeoutMs when a POSIX process that ignores SIGTERM must be escalated to SIGKILL; on Windows the same option only bounds the taskkill helper.
Keep the ChildProcess handle and call killTree(child.pid) promptly, because a pid can be reused after the process exits.
Never call killTree(process.pid); it throws RangeError. On Windows, killing an ancestor terminates the current process.
